title: PRISM: Primitive Routing via In-context Skill Mixing for Retentive VLA Adaptation
summary: The authors found that low-rank updates trained for individual skills occupied a distinguishable subspace and that a composite-task update concentrated roughly half its energy there, unlike a matched random-rotation control. PRISM then stored skill adapters as reusable primitives and routed among them. Benchmark and robot task results are separate from this representation result.
ai_technology: Vision-language model-conditioned router with frozen low-rank skill adapters
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: A composite-task update concentrated roughly half its Frobenius energy in the per-skill subspace, versus near-zero for a matched random-rotation control. RoboCasa365 and an AgileX PIPER setup were used for task evaluation.
evidence.unknown: The representation result is limited to the reported model and task setup; broader generalization is not established.
evidence.ai_role: The authors measured whether low-rank updates trained for individual manipulation skills occupy a shared parameter subspace, then proposed PRISM to preserve skill adapters as primitives and combine them with a vision-language-model-conditioned router.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
